court: Washington State Board of Tax Appeals
title: NICK URAGA and LESLEY GOODSON v. Washington Dept. of Revenue (BTA Docket No. 00-065)
text:
BEFORE THE BOARD OF TAX APPEALS
STATE OF WASHINGTON
NICK URAGA and )
LESLEY GOODSON, )
Docket No. 00- 065
Appellants, )
RE: Property Tax Appeal
v. ) Destroyed Property
KEN MADSEN, ) FINAL DECISION
Pierce County )
Assessor/ Treasurer, )
Respondent. )
This matter came before the Board of Tax Appeals ( Board) for a
formal hearing on August 28, 2001. Nick Uraga appeared for Appel-
lants, Nick Uraga and Lesley Goodson ( Owners). David Prather, Deputy
Prosecuting Attorney, appeared for Respondent, Ken Madsen, Pierce
County Assessor/ Treasurer ( Assessor).
This Board heard the testimony, reviewed the evidence, and
considered the arguments made on behalf of both parties. This Board
now makes its decision as follows:
VALUATION FOR THE 1999 ASSESSMENT YEAR
BOARD OF BOARD OF
EQUALIZATION TAX APPEALS
PARCEL NO. VALUATION VALUATION
5930030350 NOT EXEMPT NOT EXEMPT
OPINION
This is an appeal from a decision of the Pierce County Board of
Equalization denying the Owners' application for a destroyed property

1 exemption ( RCW 84. 70. 010, et. seq.). The Owners had built their home
2 in violation of neighborhood covenants. Shortly after the valuation
3 date, the Pierce County Superior Court prohibited the Owners from
4 occupying the home, and ordered it torn down to the foundation. The
5 home remained standing—but unoccupied and boarded up—pending appeal.
6 We conclude the destroyed property exemption does not apply to a home
7 which is under a judicial order of destruction so long as the home
8 remains physically intact while an appeal is pending. We affirm the
9 decision of the Board of Equalization.
10
11 FACTS
12
13 The essential facts are not in dispute. The Owners built their
14 home beginning in 1998 in a subdivision overlooking the Tacoma
15 Narrows. The neighborhood covenants required a roof pitch no greater
16 than 2 feet of rise for every 12 feet of run, except where the
17 subdivision' s architectural control committee determined that a
18 greater roof pitch would not impair or destroy the view of neighboring
19 properties. For reasons which are not relevant to the issue before
20 us, the Owners did not receive the approval of the architectural
21 control committee before constructing the home. The neighbors sued,
22 and on August 10, 1999, the Pierce County Superior Court verbally
23 prohibited the Owners from occupying the home, and ordered it torn
24 down to its foundation. The verbal order was reduced to writing and
25 entered as a judgment on December 3, 1999.
26
27
FINAL DECISION - Page 2 Docket No. 00- 065

1 The Assessor had assessed the home in 1999 as new construction,
2 with a valuation date of July 31, 1999. At the time the Assessor made
3 his valuation, he considered the home 90 percent complete. He did not
4 know of the lawsuit. He sent a Change of Value notice to the Owners
5 in September 1999, listing an improvement value of $ 236, 000. The
6 Owners did not timely appeal this valuation to the Board of
7 Equalization, as permitted by RCW 84. 40. 038. Instead, after the
8 Superior Court entered its written order in December, 1999, the Owners
9 filed an application with the Assessor claiming a destroyed property
10 exemption pursuant to RCW Ch. 84. 70. The Assessor denied the
11 application because the home remained standing. The Board of
12 Equalization affirmed, stating:
13 This Board determines that lack of occupancy does not alone
effect the value of the property. While on court appeal,
14 the structure was standing of 7- 31- 99, and is still
standing.
15
16 ANALYSIS AND CONCLUSIONS
17
18 Since 1974 Washington has provided relief to property owners
19 whose property has been destroyed in whole or in part during the
20 assessment year. The relief is in the form of a reduction in the
21 property' s assessed value, applied on a pro rata basis depending on
22 the date the property was damaged or destroyed. The statute, RCW
23 84. 70. 010, provides in relevant part:
24 1) If, on or before December 31 in any calendar year, any
real or personal property placed upon the assessment roll of
25 that year is destroyed in whole or in part, or is in an area
that has been declared a disaster area by the governor and
26 has been reduced in value by more than twenty percent as a
result of a natural disaster, the assessed value of such
27 property shall be reduced for that assessment year by an
amount determined by taking the assessed value of such
FINAL DECISION - Page 3 Docket No. 00- 065

1 taxable property before destruction or reduction in value
and deduct therefrom the true and fair value of the
2 remaining property after destruction or reduction in value.
3
4
The Owners argue that their home has been " destroyed" within the
5
meaning of the statute because as of August 10, 1999 they could not
6
occupy it, and were under a court order to tear it down to the
7
foundation. The Owners cite the definition of " destroyed" from the
8
Random House Dictionary: "... to reduce to...a useless form or remains...to
9
render ineffective or useless...." They contend that the Superior
10
Court' s oral ruling prohibiting occupancy rendered their home useless
11
as of August 10, 1999, effectively " destroying" it.
12
13
The Assessor also cites the Random House Dictionary definition of
14
destroy". He argues that although the Superior Court' s order might
15
have rendered the property useless, it did not " destroy" the Owners'
16
property because the Owners had no property right to build the home in
17
violation of the neighborhood covenants in the first instance. The
18
Assessor thus focuses not on the physical components of the property,
19
but on the intangible property rights associated with the ownership of
20
the property. The Assessor further argues that even if the Superior
21
Court' s order " destroyed" the property, the destruction did not occur
22
until December 3, 1999, when the court reduced its oral decision to
23
its final written judgment. State v. Dailey, 93 Wn. 2d 454 ( 1980).
24
25
We begin our analysis by noting that the issue is one of
26
statutory construction of a statute granting an exemption from
27
taxation. Our duty is to ascertain and give effect to the purpose and
FINAL DECISION - Page 4 Docket No. 00- 065

1 intent of the legislature, as expressed in the act. Burlington
2 Northern, Inc. v. Johnston, 89 Wn. 2d 321 ( 1977). Legislative intent
3 is to be first deduced from the statutory language. In re Lyon' s
4 Estate, 83 Wn. 2d 105 ( 1973). The words of a statute, unless otherwise
5 defined, must be given their ordinary meaning. Pope & Talbot, Inc. v.
6 State Dept. of Revenue, 90 Wn. 2d 191 ( 1978). In the case of
7 ambiguity, statutes granting an exemption from taxation should be
8 strictly, but fairly, construed against the claim of exemption. Group
9 Health Co- op of Puget Sound, Inc. v. Washington State Tax Com' n, 72
10 Wn. 2d 422 ( 1967).
11
12 The common everyday meaning of the term " destroy" is set out in
13 Webster' s Third New International Dictionary, Unabridged ( 1971), as
14 follows:
15 1. To ruin the structure, or organic existence of, or
condition of, as: a: to pull or tear down: RAZE,
16 DEMOLISH...c: to ruin completely or injure or mutilate
beyond possibility of use ( as be tearing, breaking,
17 burning, erosion.... Destroy implies any force that
smashes, tears down or apart, kills, annihilates
18 destroy a house> < destroy a document by burning it>
destroy a friendship by deceit> < destroy a bridge by
19 blowing it up.>
20
The term " destroy" thus means more than merely " rendering useless."
21
It implies physical demolition beyond possibility of further use.
22
This is the sense that the Assessor and the Board of Equalization
23
understood the term, and we agree. The purpose of the destroyed
24
property exemption, is to eliminate the perceived unfairness of
25
requiring a property owner to shoulder the burden of supporting
26
government services ( e. g., police and fire protection) which do not,
27
and cannot, benefit the owner' s property. So long as the property
FINAL DECISION - Page 5 Docket No. 00- 065

1 remains in existence it benefits from the full range of governmental
2 services. Therefore, a grant of exemption is inconsistent with the
3 purpose of the exemption. We thus conclude that the term " destroyed
4 property" is limited to property which is physically demolished in
5 whole or in part.
6
7 Further, we are far from convinced that the Owner' s property has
8 been " destroyed" in any sense of the term by the Superior Court' s
9 order. As of the close of the assessment year, December 31, 1999, the
10 Superior Court' s order was on appeal, and its effect had been stayed.
11 The Owners understandably hoped that the order would be reversed on
12 appeal, or at least modified in such a manner that most of the
13 structure would remain in existence. Thus, even if the term
14 destroyed" is understood to mean " rendered useless," the Owners' home
15 had not been finally, irrevocably, and certainly placed in that
16 condition as of the close of assessment year 1999. So long as an
17 appeal remains pending, the property cannot qualify for the destroyed
18 property exemption.
19
20 For the foregoing reasons, we uphold the determination of the
21 Board of Equalization.
22
23
24
25 FINDINGS OF FACT
26 1. This is an appeal from a decision of the Pierce County Board of
27 Equalization. The Owners filed their Notice of Appeal with this Board
FINAL DECISION - Page 6 Docket No. 00- 065

1 within 30 days of the filing of the Board of Equalization' s written
2 decision. The Assessor requested that the proceeding be held as a
3 formal appeal, pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act, RCW Ch.
4 34. 05.
5
6 2. The property which is the subject of this appeal is a single
7 family home located at 2512 N. Vista View Dr., Tacoma, Washington.
8 The Owners built their home beginning in 1998. The neighborhood
9 covenants required a roof pitch no greater than 2 feet of rise for
10 every 12 feet of run, except where the subdivision' s architectural
11 control committee determined that a greater roof pitch would not
12 impair or destroy the view of neighboring properties.
13
14 3. The Owners did not receive the approval of the architectural
15 control committee before constructing the home. The Owners' neighbors
16 filed an action in court seeking to enjoin the construction of the
17 home. On August 10, 1999, the Pierce County Superior Court verbally
18 prohibited the Owners from occupying the home, and ordered it torn
19 down to its foundation. The verbal order was reduced to writing and
20 entered as a judgment on December 3, 1999. The Owners filed a
21 supersedeas bond and appealed the Superior Court' s decision to the
22 Court of Appeals. As of the date of the hearing, the Court of Appeals
23 had rendered a decision upholding the Superior Court' s order, and the
24 case was on appeal to the Washington Supreme Court. The home remains
25 standing, but it is boarded up and unoccupied.
26
27
FINAL DECISION - Page 7 Docket No. 00- 065

1 4. The Assessor had assessed the home in 1999 as new construction,
2 with a valuation date of July 31, 1999. At the time the Assessor made
3 his valuation, he considered the home 90 percent complete. He did not
4 know of the lawsuit. He sent a Change of Value notice to the Owners
5 in September 1999, listing an improvement value of $ 236, 000. After
6 the Superior Court entered its written order in December, 1999, the
7 Owners filed an application with the Assessor claiming a destroyed
8 property exemption pursuant to RCW Ch. 84. 70. The Assessor denied the
9 application because the home remained standing. The Board of
10 Equalization affirmed the Assessor' s decision.
11
12 Any Conclusion of Law which should be deemed a Finding of Fact is
13 hereby adopted as such.
14
15 From these findings, this Board comes to these
16
17 CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
18
19 1. The Board has jurisdiction over the parties and subject matter of
20 this appeal.
21
22 2. The legal issue is one of statutory construction of a statute
23 granting an exemption from taxation. The Board is required to adhere
24 to the rules of statutory construction. The main purpose of statutory
25 construction is to ascertain and give effect to the purpose and intent
26 of the legislature. Legislative intent is to be first deduced from
27 the statutory language.
FINAL DECISION - Page 8 Docket No. 00- 065

1
2 3. The words of a statute, unless otherwise defined, must be given
3 their ordinary meaning. In the case of ambiguity, statutes granting
4 an exemption from taxation should be strictly, but fairly, construed
5 against the claim of exemption.
6
7 4. The purpose of the destroyed property exemption is to eliminate
8 the perceived unfairness of requiring a property owner to shoulder the
9 burden of supporting government services ( e. g., police and fire
10 protection) which do not, and cannot, benefit the owner' s property.
11 So long as the property remains in existence it benefits from the full
12 range of governmental services. Therefore, a grant of exemption is
13 inconsistent with the purpose of the exemption.
14
15 5. The term " destroy" as used in the destroyed property exemption,
16 RCW 84. 70. 010, means physical demolition beyond possibility of further
17 use. The term " destroyed property" as used in RCW Ch. 84. 70 is
18 limited to property which is physically demolished in whole or in
19 part.
20
21 6. The Owners' home does not qualify for the destroyed property
22 exemption, RCW Ch. 84. 70, because it was physically in existence as of
23 the last day of the 1999 assessment year and because the judicial
24 order requiring it to be torn down to its foundation was stayed
25 pending appeal.
26
27
FINAL DECISION - Page 9 Docket No. 00- 065

7. The decision of the Pierce County Board of Equalization should be
affirmed.
Any Finding of Fact which should be deemed a Conclusion of Law is
hereby adopted as such.
From these conclusions, this Board enters this
DECISION
In accordance with RCW 84. 08. 130, this Board sustains the
determination of the Pierce County Board of Equalization
The Pierce County Assessor/ Treasurer is hereby directed that the
assessment and tax rolls of Pierce County are to accord with and give
full effect to the provisions of this decision.
DATED this day of 2001.
